dedupe_keys.name: image integrated model to assess the global environment pbl

description: IMAGE, the Integrated Model to Assess the Global Environment, is an integrated assessment modelling framework that simulates the environmental consequences of human activities worldwide by linking models of land use and agriculture, energy, climate and policy. It explores long-term pathways for problems such as climate change, biodiversity loss and human well-being, and the response strategies to them. It is developed by the IMAGE team under the authority of PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency, has been developed since the 1980s, is part of the Integrated Assessment Modeling Consortium, and has been reviewed by international advisory boards; version 3.3 was released in 2022. Coverage is global, by world regions and on land use grids. The model is documented on a wiki and in the IMAGE 3.0 book; results are available free through the IMAGE data viewer (USS) with the Shared Socioeconomic Pathway scenarios, global land use maps, the IAMC scenario database and renewable energy potential data. Caveats: the model code itself is not offered for download on the pages read, so users rely on PBL runs and published scenarios. For simulation it provides consistent long-term scenarios of crop demand, land use and climate that set boundary conditions for agricultural and infrastructure climate adaptation studies. It is related to the MAGNET record in this catalogue, an economic model often linked with IMAGE.
